program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 per quarter: Tuition $4,574 + Student Service Fee $448 + Nonresident Supplemental Tuition $5,034 = $10,056 x 6 quarters (2 yrs). Excludes campus-based fees, tech fee and health insurance.
program.deadline_note: Graduate Division program page: Fall 2027 final deadline Wednesday, December 16, 2026; no priority deadline. Fall admission only.
program.gre: not accepted: 'The department does not currently require the GRE for any applicants'; do not upload scores, they will not be reviewed
program.funding_note: 'MS students may apply for TA positions each quarter and may be employed as GSRs upon availability with a faculty member.'

research_fit_note: The thesis plan (committee of three, public defense, up to 12 units of 596/598 research) lets an MS student do supervised research with UCSB's crypto/security faculty; no official MS-to-PhD pathway was stated.
notes: Length comes from the 2022-23 CS Graduate Handbook ('typically complete their degree within two years', min 3 quarters), not a current page. App fee $135 for US citizens/PR ($155 others). NRST included per instructions; he may qualify as a CA resident. | RESIDENCY: total uses nonresident tuition as specified; Sahmoud lives in Pasadena, so as a California resident the Nonresident Supplemental Tuition would likely not apply (resident tuition is much lower; see tuition_url).

program.name: MS in Computer Science (Computer and Information Sciences), thesis track
program.length: 2 yrs (30 credits)
program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 program rate $1,510 per credit x 30 credits (rate stated on the CIS MS page and the Graduate College CS program page; UD lists no separate resident/nonresident graduate rate; the standard UD graduate base rate is $1,149/credit but programs may vary).
program.deadline_note: Graduate College program page shows 'January 31' priority consideration and 'August 18' final deadline for Fall (no year shown). Decisions are rolling.
program.gre: optional: 'GRE test scores are optional and not required for admission' (CIS admissions page); the CIS MS page still lists minimums of 153V/155Q/4.0 AW
program.funding_note: 'most of the financial aid awards are made to PhD students and occasionally to strong MS students'; outstanding MS applicants may be considered for aid; admission does not guarantee funding. TA consideration requires TOEFL 100+ (international).

research_fit_note: 30-credit MS with a thesis track (6 thesis credits + 12 breadth + 12 elective) that the department describes as for students who may consider a PhD; all students start non-thesis and enter the thesis track once their advisory committee is approved, so lining up a faculty advisor early is key.
notes: Thesis track not guaranteed at admission ('Admission does not guarantee that a student can follow the thesis track'). GRE conflict between the CIS admissions page (optional) and the CIS MS page (lists minimum scores). No dedicated security/crypto MS was found among CIS programs (other colleges not exhaustively checked).

program.name: MS in Computer Science (thesis option)
program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 (Fall 2026/Spring 2027) nonresident Graduate Base Rate Range I (12+ hrs) $14,063/semester + Engineering 'MS Engineering and Computer Science' tuition differential $2,474/semester = $16,537/semester x 3 semesters (36 credit hours at 12/semester). Alternative: 4 semesters at 9 hrs (Range II: $9,375 + $1,649) = $44,096. Tuition only; fees and assessments excluded.
program.deadline_note: CS admissions page lists 'January 15: recommended deadline for MS applicants' and 'February 15: all PhD and MS applicants' with no year; mapped to the Fall 2027 cycle (same page says 'MS applications must be submitted by Feb. 15, 2027' for the fee waiver). Final deadline 2027-02-15.
program.gre: Conflicting official pages: CS admissions page says 'GRE general test scores are required for all MS applicants, with the exception of UIC graduates'; the CS MS admissions page says U.S. degree holders are not required to submit GRE and it is required for degrees received outside the U.S.
program.funding_note: CS admissions page: 'Most CS graduate students, including masters, are eligible for financial support, including teaching assistantships (TA), research assistantships (RA), and graduate fellowships.' Assistantships of 25-67% time carry a tuition exemption (CS funding page). Not guaranteed for MS (the guaranteed funded appointment described is for PhD students).

research_fit_note: The MS has coursework-only, project, and thesis options; the department says the thesis option is 'strongly advised for students who may be interested in pursuing a PhD in the future.' No formal MS-to-PhD transfer pathway is stated.
notes: length null: no official program length found (36 semester hours minimum). app_fee: Graduate College domestic admission page states $80 (no effective term given; some older department pages say $70); College of Engineering sponsors MS fee waivers for applications submitted by Feb 15, 2027 after attending a CS info session; the $100 credential fee for international credentials is not waived. Tuition table is a PDF on uofi.box.com linked from the registrar page. GRE policy conflicts between two official CS pages; verify with cs-info@uic.edu.

school: University of Massachusetts Amherst (Manning College of Information & Computer Sciences)

program.name: MS in Computer Science - On Campus (with 6-credit Master's Project research option)
program.length: 2-4 years ('Plan on two to four years to finish your degree, depending on your course load')
program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 out-of-state per-semester tuition by credit load (Bursar): 9 credits $17,806.50 x 3 semesters + 3 credits $5,935.50 = $59,355 for 30 credits. Tuition only (fees excluded). CICS tuition page separately states 'Total Tuition & Mandatory Fees ... Out-of-State/International: $60,750'.
program.deadline_note: CICS MS page: 'Fall Enrollment (early decision) December 15, 2026'; 'Fall Enrollment (regular decision) March 15, 2027'.
program.gre: Optional: 'The GRE test is optional for the MS program.'
program.funding_note: None: 'Graduate assistantships are not available to Manning CICS; however, MS students can seek part-time employment opportunities across campus.' Terminal master's students (cohorts since Fall 2016) are ineligible for assistantships in the college or elsewhere on campus except in extraordinary circumstances.

alt_programs.name: MS in Computer Science - Security concentration
alt_programs.note: Concentration within the same non-thesis MS emphasizing security-related courses.

research_fit_note: The MS is officially 'a non-thesis degree,' but students interested in research are encouraged to do independent study after their first semester and can take a 6-credit Master's Project (a research project or paper with one or two professors, often spanning two semesters). No MS-to-PhD pathway for terminal MS students was stated.
notes: thesis set to 'yes' only because of the 6-credit research Master's Project; there is no formal thesis. App fee $90 from the Graduate School how-to-apply page. 30 credits required.

program.name: MS in Computer Science (thesis option), Kahlert School of Computing
program.length: typically 2 yrs (30 credit hours)
program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 graduate nonresident per semester: zero-hour tuition $3,830.64 + $1,171.51/credit. 4 semesters x $3,830.64 + 30 credits x $1,171.51 = $50,467.86. Excludes mandatory fees and the College of Engineering course differential (~$101.70/credit on the 2026-27 schedule; the CS financial page cites $87.05).
program.deadline_note: 'The deadline for Fall 2027 applications is December 15, 2026.' Fall admission only.
program.gre: optional: 'Optional for Masters and Ph.D. Applicants'
program.funding_note: RAs appointed directly by faculty on external grants; TAs via the School's TA portal but it 'cannot guarantee a TA position to new students'; master's students limited to 2 years (4 semesters) of tuition benefit.

alt_programs.name: MS in Computing, Secure Computing track
alt_programs.note: Track 'rigorously prepares graduate students for careers in cybersecurity research and development'; open to MS and PhD students.

research_fit_note: MS applicants choose a Thesis or Non-Thesis option on the application, and RA/TA appointments carry tuition benefit, so a thesis MS with crypto/security faculty (or the Secure Computing track) is a realistic research on-ramp; no official MS-to-PhD path was stated.
notes: 30 credit hours taken from the BS/MS page (applies to the MS generally); thesis credit details are in the yearly handbook (Google Drive), not reviewed. App fee $55 domestic ($65 international). Utah residency may be obtainable after the first year, which would lower cost.

program.name: MS in Computer Sciences (traditional MS/PhD program, optional thesis)
program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 UW-Madison Graduate full-time nonresident tuition $12,027.20/semester x 4 semesters (30-credit MS; part-time is under 8 credits). 3 semesters would be $36,081.60. Tuition only; segregated fees ($849.74/semester) excluded. Bursar states graduate tuition rates unchanged for 2026-27.
program.deadline_note: CS admissions page shows 'Application Deadline: December 15' with no year for the traditional MS/PhD program (fall admission only); mapped to the Fall 2027 cycle.
program.gre: Not required ('GRE test scores are NOT required for admission to Department of Computer Sciences graduate programs'); submitted scores may be considered.
program.funding_note: CS admissions page (traditional MS/PhD): 'We offer financial support to a large number of our admitted students in the form of teaching assistantships, research assistantships and/or competitive fellowships. Decisions on financial support are made at the same time as admission decisions.'

alt_programs.name: Computer Sciences: Professional Program MS (PMP)
alt_programs.note: Coursework-based professional MS; February 15 deadline; less suited to a research path.

research_fit_note: Single applicant pool for MS and PhD; admitted MS students do not need to reapply to continue to the PhD, but 'continuing for a PhD is contingent upon successfully completing the department's PhD Qualifying Process.' Optional 6-credit master's thesis (CS 790) 'could serve as a basis toward subsequent doctoral work.'
notes: length null: guide.wisc.edu (the official Guide with degree requirements) was unreachable (connection timeout/refused), so no official time-to-degree was confirmed; 30-credit minimum taken from the CS 2024-25 Graduate Handbook (the 2026-27 handbook defers to the Guide). App fee $75 (+$6 international processing) from the Graduate School apply page; one fee covers up to 3 programs. Department says: 'Do not apply to both MS and PhD programs!'

program.deadline_note: Dept FAQ and program page show 'Fall: March 15' (no year); Spring Sept 15.

program.funding_note: Regular-track students "are eligible for departmental scholarships, teaching and research assistantships. Competition for the few slots available is stiff." RAs come from individual faculty with openings. Professional track not eligible.

alt_programs.name: M.S. in Computer Science, Professional Track

school: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University

program.length: Two years; minimum 30 credits (21 graded + CS 5994 research/thesis)
program.tuition_basis: 2026-27 Graduate Blacksburg non-Virginia-resident tuition, 9+ credits, $16,790.50/semester x 4 semesters (comprehensive fees, Commonwealth Facility fee, and $262.50/semester Engineering supplemental fee excluded)
program.deadline_note: Dept page: 'Fall 2027 Admission ... MS Program: Application Deadline: December 1, 2026 (Blacksburg & Northern Virginia campuses)'; decisions typically by March 1, 2027.

alt_programs.name: Master of Engineering (MEng) in Computer Science & Applications
alt_programs.note: Coursework/project degree, mainly in the D.C. area; not a research path. Switching MEng to MS needs a faculty member to commit GRA funding.

alt_programs.name: Ph.D. in Computer Science & Applications
alt_programs.note: Deadline 2026-12-01; direct entry from bachelor's allowed; MS 'on the way' available.

VT's MS is thesis-only for MS students ('We no longer allow MS students to do the MS coursework option'), and MS admission is limited by faculty advising capacity.
notes: gre null: the VT Graduate School 'does not require entrance tests' but defers to departments, and no current CS-department statement of the MS GRE policy was found on the pages fetched. VT Graduate School app fee $75. The degree is officially named Computer Science & Applications (CSA).

program.deadline_note: Priority deadline 'January 10 for fall semester' (no year); later applications still reviewed but funding is less likely.
